name: Alcohol-to-jet SAF
applications: sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel from ethanol or isobutanol
principle: Ethanol or isobutanol is dehydrated to light olefins, which are oligomerised into longer chains, hydrogenated and fractionated into jet and diesel range paraffins. Any low-carbon alcohol can be the feed, including ethanol from wastes or gas fermentation.

reference_plants.name: LanzaJet Freedom Pines Fuels, Soperton, Georgia
reference_plants.capacity: 10 million gal/yr SAF and renewable diesel from ethanol
reference_plants.status: opened January 2024; described as the first ATJ SAF plant

advantages: Alcohol feeds are widely available and can be low carbon
Large potential feedstock base beyond lipids
limitations: Product cost tied to ethanol price
